<a id="ingredient-identity-and-scope"></a>
## What counts as strawberries

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-can-be-transferred-between-those-materials-and-what-requires-a-separate-answer"></a>

This page covers strawberries in 5 forms kept separate in every comparison: strawberries, as sold (213 results), strawberries, frozen (8 results), strawberries, juice (2 results), strawberries, canned (1 result) and strawberries, dried (1 result).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-strawberries" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-strawberries-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of strawberries, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

<a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach strawberries

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach strawberries comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Strawberries, as sold from frozen product, Poland retail/official control had lead higher at 11 µg/kg, against 9 µg/kg for fresh product, Poland retail/official control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.



<a id="ranges-by-source-region-and-variety"></a>
## Which forms and regions measured lower

<a id="how-do-concentrations-vary-by-origin-growing-conditions-variety-and-harvest-period"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-014"></a>

<a id="hmi-ing-015"></a>

Targeted strawberries, as sold samples in EURO had aluminium lower at 516 µg/kg, against 905 µg/kg for EURO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, Zn across 4 groups of strawberries ranged from 1,060 µg/kg (vegetable and fruit market; washed with 10% acetic acid vinegar) to 1,360 µg/kg (amateur farmers; washed with 10% acetic acid vinegar); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>

<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed strawberries in the same study and group. Strawberries, canned (Fruits, Riyadh city markets, May 2009) had lead higher at 30 µg/kg, against 17 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (strawberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, strawberries, juice (PAHO) had cadmium lower at 3 µg/kg, against 16 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (strawberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for strawberries

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Avoiding exposed growing areas lowered the metal measured in the studies available, but no study measured the cost or supply effect of doing so.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-strawberries" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-strawberries" data-question="How do heavy metals get into strawberries?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into strawberries?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, strawberries from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than strawberries from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Strawberries, as sold from frozen product, Poland retail/official control had lead higher at 11 µg/kg, against 9 µg/kg for fresh product, Poland retail/official control in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rusin M, Domagalska J, Rogala D, Razzaghi M, Szymala I · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Concentration of cadmium and lead in vegetables and fruits</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rusin2021-vegetables-fruits-cadmium-lead-poland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-types-of-strawberries-have-the-lowest-levels" data-anchor="which-types-of-strawberries-have-the-lowest-levels" data-question="Which types of strawberries have the lowest levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which types of strawberries have the lowest levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

For cadmium, the HMI reference median was lowest for strawberries, frozen (8.5 µg/kg) and highest for strawberries, as sold (30 µg/kg); forms differ in water content, so this compares foods as sold or eaten, not uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-strawberries" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-strawberries" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in strawberries?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in strawberries?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, strawberries, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in PAHO (2.3 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (1,120 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in PAHO (7 µg/kg) and the highest in EURO (50 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same strawberries.<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Strawberries, canned (Fruits, Riyadh city markets, May 2009) had lead higher at 30 µg/kg, against 17 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (strawberries, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Al Othman ZA · 2010</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Lead Contamination in Selected Foods from Riyadh City Market and Estimation of the Daily Intake</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Molecules 2010, 15, 7482-7497</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/othman2010-riyadh-market-foods-lead">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>
